title: What Piles Up
endLine: A broken step announces itself by what piles up behind it.

scenes.tts: Burned amino acids split by atom: nitrogen is caged as urea, and carbon enters through seven doors. Now picture urine that turns black. In nineteen oh two, Archibald Garrod argued that this disease, alkaptonuria, is inherited. How can a color point to one broken step?
scenes.narration: Burned amino acids split by atom: nitrogen is caged as urea, and carbon enters through seven doors. Now picture urine that turns black. In 1902, Archibald Garrod argued that this disease, alkaptonuria, is inherited. How can a color point to one broken step?
scenes.caption: Burned amino acids split by atom: nitrogen is caged as urea, and carbon enters through seven doors. Now picture urine that turns black. In 1902, Archibald Garrod argued that this disease, alkaptonuria, is inherited. How can a color point to one broken step?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's recycling-center world and colour map without a reset: carbon skeletons are BLUE blocks on a lower conveyor, nitrogen is GOLD tokens, the turning five-station urea wheel and the seven-door central-metabolism hub are the same objects as before. New in this film: a dark RED blood lane running along the bottom of the frame, a pale YELLOW urine flask at lower right, and BROKEN stations drawn in bright RED. A small 'schematic' tag stays at bottom right throughout. During the first sentence, a quick recap: on 'nitrogen is caged as urea', a GOLD token rides into the turning urea wheel (upper left) and leaves in a capsule labelled 'urea'; on 'carbon enters through seven doors', a BLUE block rides the lower conveyor into the seven-door hub (right). On 'Now picture', the camera pushes in on the YELLOW urine flask, which fills the centre at about 60% of frame height; its liquid slowly darkens from yellow to black while the world keeps moving faintly behind. On 'nineteen oh two', a plain tag '1902 · Garrod: inherited' appears beside the flask. On the question, large white text across the top: 'How can a colour find a broken step?' A small RED question mark pulses beside the darkening flask.
Title 'What Piles Up' fades in above the flask for 2 seconds while the question text fades out. The black liquid in the flask swirls slowly; the conveyor behind keeps rolling.

scenes.tts: Each carbon skeleton reaches its door through a line of enzymes. Every enzyme does one step. Some steps need a vitamin helper, a cofactor. The cofactor is a fingerprint: it tells you what kind of step it is.
scenes.narration: Each carbon skeleton reaches its door through a line of enzymes. Every enzyme does one step. Some steps need a vitamin helper, a cofactor. The cofactor is a fingerprint: it tells you what kind of step it is.
scenes.caption: Each carbon skeleton reaches its door through a line of enzymes. Every enzyme does one step. Some steps need a vitamin helper, a cofactor. The cofactor is a fingerprint: it tells you what kind of step it is.
scenes.visual: The camera pulls back from the flask (it shrinks back to lower right) and zooms onto the lower conveyor so the carbon line fills about 65% of the frame height. Show, then tell: the conveyor resolves into a row of three machine stations in pale grey, each labelled 'enzyme', with BLUE carbon blocks entering at left and the seven-door hub at right. On 'Every enzyme does one step', a BLUE block passes through each station and changes shape slightly at each one (one notch added or moved per station). On 'vitamin helper', a small GREEN tool token slots into the middle station; on 'fingerprint', the tool token glows and a stamp-like print of its outline appears above the station, labelled 'cofactor = fingerprint'. Blocks keep flowing station to station throughout. On screen: conveyor, three stations, blocks, tool token, hub, flask (six things).

scenes.tts: Take the succinyl coenzyme A door. Valine, isoleucine, methionine and threonine are broken down to propionyl coenzyme A. A biotin enzyme carboxylates it to methylmalonyl coenzyme A. Then a B twelve enzyme rearranges that into succinyl coenzyme A. Biotin means carboxylation. B twelve means rearrangement.
scenes.narration: Take the succinyl-CoA door. Valine, isoleucine, methionine and threonine are broken down to propionyl-CoA. A biotin enzyme carboxylates it to methylmalonyl-CoA. Then a B12 enzyme rearranges that into succinyl-CoA. Biotin means carboxylation. B12 means rearrangement.
scenes.caption: Take the succinyl-CoA door. Valine, isoleucine, methionine and threonine are broken down to propionyl-CoA. A biotin enzyme carboxylates it to methylmalonyl-CoA. Then a B12 enzyme rearranges that into succinyl-CoA. Biotin means carboxylation. B12 means rearrangement.
scenes.visual: Keep the same line of stations, now leading to one lit door of the hub labelled 'succinyl-CoA'. On the four amino-acid names, four BLUE blocks (each tagged with its name: 'valine', 'isoleucine', 'methionine', 'threonine') ride in on converging tracks, and each in turn becomes a BLUE block labelled 'propionyl-CoA' at the same point; the four tags fade, and the front block moves on. On 'biotin enzyme', the middle station gains its GREEN tool token labelled 'biotin'; the block passes through and a small extra BLUE knob (one carbon unit, schematic) clicks onto it, and its label changes to 'methylmalonyl-CoA'. On 'B twelve enzyme', the next station gains a PURPLE tool token labelled 'B12'; the block passes through and its parts visibly shuffle into a new arrangement (same pieces, new order), and its label changes to 'succinyl-CoA' as it enters the lit door. On the last two sentences, the GREEN token stamps 'carboxylation' and the PURPLE token stamps 'rearrangement' above their stations. No molecular structures; blocks are plain shapes.

scenes.tts: Now jam one station. Its enzyme is defective, but molecules keep arriving from upstream. Which will rise: the molecule the station takes in, or the one it makes?
scenes.narration: Now jam one station. Its enzyme is defective, but molecules keep arriving from upstream. Which will rise: the molecule the station takes in, or the one it makes?
scenes.caption: Now jam one station. Its enzyme is defective, but molecules keep arriving from upstream. Which will rise: the molecule the station takes in, or the one it makes?
scenes.visual: Same line of three stations. On 'jam', the middle station turns bright RED and its rollers stop, labelled 'defective enzyme'; the other stations keep running. BLUE blocks keep arriving from the left at the same rate and slow as they reach the RED station. Two answer panels grow above the line: one on the left of the RED station labelled 'what it takes in', one on the right labelled 'what it makes', each with an empty level bar (schematic). Large white question card across the top: 'Which one rises?' Do not show any pile yet.

Predict pause. Hold the exact layout for 4.5 seconds: the RED station stopped, the two answer panels with empty level bars, the question card on screen. BLUE blocks creep forward slowly from the left, and a circular thinking timer traces one turn. Reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: The one it takes in. With nowhere to go, it piles up behind the jam. It can spill out into the blood and the urine. A broken step announces itself by what piles up behind it.
scenes.narration: The one it takes in. With nowhere to go, it piles up behind the jam. It can spill out into the blood and the urine. A broken step announces itself by what piles up behind it.
scenes.caption: The one it takes in. With nowhere to go, it piles up behind the jam. It can spill out into the blood and the urine. A broken step announces itself by what piles up behind it.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. Show, then tell: BLUE blocks stack up in a growing heap on the left of the RED station; the left panel's level bar rises in step with the heap (schematic). On 'spill out', blocks overflow the heap and drop down into the dark RED blood lane, where they drift along; some of them flow into the YELLOW urine flask at lower right, which starts to cloud. On the guiding sentence, the heap glows and a bold label appears over it: 'the pile-up points here', with an arrow from the heap to the RED station. The right panel's bar stays low. Blood-lane drift and heap growth continue throughout.

scenes.tts: In P K U, phenylalanine hydroxylase is defective. Phenylalanine, the molecule it takes in, rises in the blood. In many countries, newborn screening looks for exactly that, in a dried blood spot taken days after birth.
scenes.narration: In PKU, phenylalanine hydroxylase is defective. Phenylalanine, the molecule it takes in, rises in the blood. In many countries, newborn screening looks for exactly that, in a dried blood spot taken days after birth.
scenes.caption: In PKU, phenylalanine hydroxylase is defective. Phenylalanine, the molecule it takes in, rises in the blood. In many countries, newborn screening looks for exactly that, in a dried blood spot taken days after birth.
scenes.visual: Relabel the same jammed line: the RED station now reads 'phenylalanine hydroxylase', a tag 'PKU' appears above it, and the heap of blocks to its left is relabelled 'phenylalanine'. On 'rises in the blood', BLUE blocks tagged 'phenylalanine' thicken in the RED blood lane and a level gauge beside the lane, labelled 'blood phenylalanine', climbs (schematic, no numbers). On 'newborn screening', the camera follows the blood lane to a small card with one dark-red dot labelled 'dried blood spot'; the dot glows where phenylalanine blocks sit in it, and a tag reads 'flags PKU'. Keep the heap and the blood lane moving. No molecular structures.

scenes.tts: In maple syrup urine disease, a branched-chain keto-acid dehydrogenase is defective. Branched-chain amino acids and their keto acids build up behind it. The urine smells of maple syrup, and the excess leucine is neurotoxic.
scenes.narration: In maple syrup urine disease, a branched-chain keto-acid dehydrogenase is defective. Branched-chain amino acids and their keto acids build up behind it. The urine smells of maple syrup, and the excess leucine is neurotoxic.
scenes.caption: In maple syrup urine disease, a branched-chain keto-acid dehydrogenase is defective. Branched-chain amino acids and their keto acids build up behind it. The urine smells of maple syrup, and the excess leucine is neurotoxic.
scenes.visual: The blood-spot card slides away. A different line, a different jam: the PKU line slides aside and a separate line of grey stations for the branched-chain amino acids takes its place; one of its stations turns RED, labelled 'branched-chain keto-acid dehydrogenase' and tagged 'MSUD'. A new heap grows to its left, made of two kinds of BLUE blocks labelled 'branched-chain amino acids' and 'keto acids'. Blocks overflow into the blood lane and reach the YELLOW urine flask; on 'smells of maple syrup', soft amber wisps curl up from the flask. On 'neurotoxic', the blocks tagged 'leucine' in the blood lane pulse and a small warning gauge labelled 'leucine excess' rises (schematic). Keep the heap, blood lane and wisps moving.

scenes.tts: The nitrogen road obeys the same rule. When the urea cycle fails, ammonia piles up. Astrocytes swell as they trap it in glutamine, and the brain swells.
scenes.narration: The nitrogen road obeys the same rule. When the urea cycle fails, ammonia piles up. Astrocytes swell as they trap it in glutamine, and the brain swells.
scenes.caption: The nitrogen road obeys the same rule. When the urea cycle fails, ammonia piles up. Astrocytes swell as they trap it in glutamine, and the brain swells.
scenes.visual: Pan up from the carbon line to the turning urea wheel from the first film (the carbon line stays faint below). GOLD nitrogen tokens arrive on the 'ammonium' cart. On 'fails', the wheel slows to a stop and turns RED; GOLD tokens heap up at its entrance, labelled 'ammonia', and the first film's danger gauge climbs. On 'Astrocytes', the heap spills into the blood lane and drifts to a simple star-shaped cell outline labelled 'astrocyte'; GOLD tokens enter it and lock onto small carts labelled 'glutamine', and the cell outline swells. On 'the brain swells', a plain rounded brain outline around the astrocyte widens slightly, labelled 'brain edema'. No molecular structures.

scenes.tts: Back to Garrod's black urine. In alkaptonuria, a molecule called homogentisate piles up. It oxidizes to a black pigment, so the urine darkens. Alkaptonuria became the first recognized inborn error of metabolism. Each such error is rare, but as a group they are not.
scenes.narration: Back to Garrod's black urine. In alkaptonuria, a molecule called homogentisate piles up. It oxidizes to a black pigment, so the urine darkens. Alkaptonuria became the first recognized inborn error of metabolism. Each such error is rare, but as a group they are not.

scenes.visual: The urea wheel returns to grey and turning; the danger gauge falls. Camera returns to the carbon line. A station on it turns RED, tagged 'alkaptonuria'. A heap grows to its left, labelled 'homogentisate'. Blocks overflow into the blood lane and into the YELLOW urine flask from the opening; on 'oxidizes', the blocks in the flask darken one by one and the liquid turns black, matching the hook. On 'first recognized inborn error', a line draws from the black flask back to the RED station, labelled 'colour → station'. On 'as a group', small RED dots light up on several other stations along the line, then dim.

scenes.tts: So read a metabolic disease like a jammed line. Find what has piled up, and the broken step sits just past it. Then ask which cofactor that step needs.
scenes.narration: So read a metabolic disease like a jammed line. Find what has piled up, and the broken step sits just past it. Then ask which cofactor that step needs.
scenes.caption: So read a metabolic disease like a jammed line. Find what has piled up, and the broken step sits just past it. Then ask which cofactor that step needs.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole world: the carbon line with its stations, the GOLD urea wheel above, the blood lane and the flask below, the seven-door hub at right, all moving. On 'jammed line', one station flashes RED and a heap forms behind it. On 'Find what has piled up', a magnifying-glass ring sweeps over the heap and slides one step right onto the RED station, labelled 'broken step'. On 'which cofactor', the GREEN 'biotin' and PURPLE 'B12' tool tokens glow on their stations. Blocks keep flowing everywhere else.

End card on the same dark ground over the dimmed but still moving world (BLUE blocks flowing along the line, the urea wheel turning). Hex waves above the line, large centred white text: 'A broken step announces itself by what piles up behind it.' A small heap of BLUE blocks pulses gently beside a RED station beneath the line; do not repeat the title.
